patch.value: Recursive self-improvement: a training loop whose every generation is tracked, gated, and invalidatable

pm-rl must be able to run a policy that improves itself: a generation collects trajectories, trains a successor, and the successor collects the next generation's trajectories. The loop is easy to run and almost impossible to trust, because every property that makes a result meaningful degrades silently as it turns. The generating policy is not recorded, so nobody can say which model produced a trajectory. The held-out set quietly becomes training data, so the score rises while capability does not. The proxy objective and the objective the programme actually cares about drift apart, and only the proxy is measured. An environment or reward edit invalidates every downstream generation, and nothing says so. None of these are training problems. They are all provenance problems, which is to say context problems, and pm already models the graph that answers them. This epic makes a generation a first-class tracked item whose parent is the generation that produced its training data, makes promotion a gated transition that refuses on contamination rather than warning about it, measures the proxy-to-held-out gap across generations as the reward-hacking signal it is, and binds the whole loop to an approved generation budget that the CLI will not advance past on its own.

A generation records its base checkpoint, generating policy, collection runs and training config as typed fields; promotion refuses when the evaluation set is reachable from the candidate's training data in the dependency graph; the proxy-to-held-out gap is reported per generation and its trend across the chain; advancing past the approved generation budget is refused and names the approval item required; an environment or reward-spec edit invalidates every downstream generation transitively; 100 percent line, branch, function and docstring coverage

author: claude

patch.value: Every artifact a verdict depends on carries an immutable content-addressed identity: environment version, reward specification version, base checkpoint, candidate tree, collection run, and each recorded score; a generation declares explicit typed edges to its parent generation, its collection runs, and the exact environment and reward-spec versions those runs used, so reverse reachability from an environment edit reaches every downstream generation; promotion refuses when the evaluation set is reachable from the candidate's training data over the declared edge types, and the refusal prints a stable path; the proxy and held-out scores are attributed identically and compared by a defined direction-aware formula; advancing past the approved promotion budget is refused and names the approval item required; pm-rl runs no trainer and registers no command until its acceptance criteria and refusal paths are implemented and tested; 100 percent line, branch, function and docstring coverage

pm-rl must be able to TRACK AND GATE a loop in which a policy improves itself: a generation collects trajectories, a trainer outside pm-rl produces a successor, and the successor collects the next generation's trajectories. pm-rl never runs the trainer, never schedules compute, and never orchestrates a job; it records what happened, refuses to let a result look valid when its provenance says otherwise, and answers the questions the loop cannot answer about itself. That boundary is deliberate and matches the package's existing no-orchestration scope. The loop is easy to run and almost impossible to trust, because every property that makes a result meaningful degrades silently as it turns. The generating policy is not recorded, so nobody can say which model produced a trajectory. The held-out set quietly becomes training data, so the score rises while capability does not. The proxy objective and the objective the programme actually cares about drift apart, and only the proxy is measured. An environment or reward edit invalidates every downstream generation, and nothing says so. None of these are training problems. They are all provenance problems, which is to say context problems, and pm already models the graph that answers them - but only if the graph carries the right edges. Reachability is not free: a parent edge from a generation to its predecessor does not connect an environment revision to the generations that used it. This epic therefore requires an explicit graph contract as its foundation, not as a later refinement.

message: Reframe scope as tracking and gating, and require an explicit graph contract

value.text:
Correcting the completion record after a review finding. Five of this epic's six children are closed: pm-rl-81oc generation lineage, pm-rl-qix7 the approved budget, pm-rl-zav1 the proxy-to-held-out gap, pm-rl-32a9 rl lineage, and pm-rl-gyrj the contamination refusal. The ten defect issues opened from the first review round are also all closed.

The epic stays OPEN on exactly one remaining child: pm-rl-0cqg, the fleet's own mandatory gates as the first sim-to-RL environment. Its criteria are candidate-tree identity, exact replay, pull-request linkage, and paired-cohort reporting. closed_at, completed_at and close_reason must not be set until that child and those criteria are complete.

This corrects an earlier statement that the remaining roadmap item was the incompatible-version ranking refusal (pm-rl-p401). p401 is real and still open, but it is NOT a child of this epic, so it is not what holds the epic open.

value.text:
Correcting a count in my earlier completion note. That note said TEN defect issues were opened from the first review round. The repository contains EIGHT: pm-rl-cnc0, pm-rl-k5xd, pm-rl-izu1, pm-rl-qdxu, pm-rl-6fb5, pm-rl-dzqc, pm-rl-o9dr and pm-rl-82qw.

The confusion was mine and is worth naming precisely, because it is a category error rather than a miscount. The review reported ten FINDINGS, rated one Critical, five Major and four lesser. I tracked those ten findings as eight ITEMS, because several findings shared one root cause and were grouped, for example the three parse and arithmetic checks that became pm-rl-dzqc. Writing ten in a sentence about issues conflated findings with items.

Everything else in that note stands and has been re-verified against the tracked files rather than from memory: five of the six original epic children are closed, pm-rl-0cqg is the single remaining open child, and closed_at, completed_at and close_reason remain unset until its criteria are met.

Note also that a single comment body is stored in both the item projection and the durable history event, so one wrong sentence appears in both places and one corrective entry fixes both.
